title: Suggests switching the initialization pattern of absl::Cleanup instances from the factory function to class template argument deduction (CTAD), in C++17 and higher.
summary: clang-tidy can fix the code that it finds. The check is in the abseil module of clang-tidy.

title: Checks for cases where addition should be performed in the absl::Time domain.
summary: When adding two values, and one is known to be an absl::Time, we can infer that the other should be interpreted as an absl::Duration of a similar scale, and make that inference explicit. clang-tidy can fix the code that it finds. The check is in the abseil module of clang-tidy.

title: Checks for comparisons which should be in the absl::Duration domain instead of the floating point or integer domains.
summary: clang-tidy can fix the code that it finds. The check is in the abseil module of clang-tidy.

title: Checks for casts of absl::Duration conversion functions, and recommends the right conversion function instead.
summary: clang-tidy can fix the code that it finds. The check is in the abseil module of clang-tidy.

title: Absl::Duration arithmetic works like it does with integers.
summary: That means that division of two absl::Duration objects returns an int64 with any fractional component truncated toward 0. See this link for more information on arithmetic with absl::Duration. clang-tidy can fix the code that it finds. The check is in the abseil module of clang-tidy.

title: Checks for cases where the floating-point overloads of various absl::Duration factory functions are called when the more-efficient integer versions could be used instead.
summary: clang-tidy can fix the code that it finds. The check is in the abseil module of clang-tidy.

title: Checks for cases where arguments to absl::Duration factory functions are scaled internally and could be changed to a different factory function.
summary: This check also looks for arguments with a zero value and suggests using absl::ZeroDuration() instead. clang-tidy can fix the code that it finds. The check is in the abseil module of clang-tidy.

title: Checks for cases where subtraction should be performed in the absl::Duration domain.
summary: When subtracting two values, and the first one is known to be a conversion from absl::Duration, we can infer that the second should also be interpreted as an absl::Duration, and make that inference explicit. clang-tidy can fix the code that it finds. The check is in the abseil module of clang-tidy.

title: Finds and fixes cases where absl::Duration values are being converted to numeric types and back again.
summary: clang-tidy can fix the code that it finds. The check is in the abseil module of clang-tidy.

title: Finds instances of absl::StrSplit() or absl::MaxSplits() where the delimiter is a single character string literal and replaces with a character.
summary: The check will offer a suggestion to change the string literal into a character. It will also catch code using absl::ByAnyChar() for just a single character and will transform that into a single character as well. clang-tidy can fix the code that it finds. The check is in the abseil module of clang-tidy.

title: Warns if code using Abseil depends on internal details.
summary: If something is in a namespace that includes the word "internal", code is not allowed to depend upon it because it's an implementation detail. They cannot friend it, include it, you mention it or refer to it in any way. The check is in the abseil module of clang-tidy.

title: Ensures code does not open namespace absl as that violates Abseil's compatibility guidelines.
summary: Code should not open namespace absl as that conflicts with Abseil's compatibility guidelines and may result in breakage. The check is in the abseil module of clang-tidy.

title: Suggests removal of unnecessary calls to absl::StrCat when the result is being passed to another call to absl::StrCat or absl::StrAppend.
summary: clang-tidy can fix the code that it finds. The check is in the abseil module of clang-tidy.

title: Flags uses of absl::StrCat() to append to a std::string.
summary: Suggests absl::StrAppend() should be used instead. clang-tidy can fix the code that it finds. The check is in the abseil module of clang-tidy.

title: Checks whether a std::string::find() or std::string::rfind() (and corresponding std::string_view methods) result is compared with 0, and suggests replacing with absl::StartsWith().
summary: This is both a readability and performance issue. clang-tidy can fix the code that it finds. The check is in the abseil module of clang-tidy.

title: Finds s.find(...) == string::npos comparisons (for various string-like types) and suggests replacing with absl::StrContains().
summary: clang-tidy can fix the code that it finds. The check is in the abseil module of clang-tidy.

title: Prefer comparisons in the absl::Time domain instead of the integer domain.
summary: clang-tidy can fix the code that it finds. The check is in the abseil module of clang-tidy.

title: Finds and fixes absl::Time subtraction expressions to do subtraction in the Time domain instead of the numeric domain.
summary: clang-tidy can fix the code that it finds. The check is in the abseil module of clang-tidy.

title: This check identifies unsafe accesses to values contained in absl::StatusOr<T> objects.
summary: Below we will refer to this type as StatusOr<T>. The check is in the abseil module of clang-tidy.
